content.text:
I replaced the toolbar at the top of the main window with a Ribbon: a gpui-kit tab bar with default styling, and the selected tab's controls in a row underneath. 89 of 90 tests pass, including a new one that switches through every tab and checks each shows only its own controls. The one failure is the palette test that was already failing. I haven't looked at it in the running app.

| Tab | Controls |
|---|---|
| **Project** (selected at launch) | Open Project button, which shows the project's name once one is open |
| **Code** | nothing yet |
| **Spec** | Build Spec, which runs `piton build` |
| **Research** | nothing yet |
| **Application** | Dark mode switch and a Settings button |

**Choices I made:**
- **Row height:** the controls row keeps its height on Code and Research, so the window below doesn't jump when you switch tabs.
- **Palette:** its Build command now reads "Build Spec" too, to match.
- **Settings button:** it now shows the label "Settings" next to the gear icon, instead of the icon alone.
- **Remembering the tab:** the selected tab isn't saved, so the app always opens on Project.

The toolbar code moved from `src/toolbar.rs` to `src/ribbon.rs`. The spec still describes the old toolbar in `MainWindowScope`, so that needs a spec-mode prompt.
